name: LIFE (Eclipse)
question: Among women with fecal incontinence, how often could the Eclipse vaginal bowel-control system be fitted and reduce leakage episodes during short-term use?

design.population: Women aged 19–75 years at six clinical sites with fecal incontinence for at least six months and at least four minor or major episodes on a two-week baseline diary underwent attempted device fitting.
design.description: Multicenter prospective open-label single-arm device study
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 541–542; Figure 2, p 543

verdictNote: The primary endpoint met its prespecified threshold among the 61 women entering treatment after fitting.
takeaway: In the single-arm LIFE study, Eclipse treatment followed successful fitting in 61/110 women. At one month, 48/61 (78.7%; 95% CI 66–88%) had at least 50% fewer fecal incontinence episodes, exceeding the prespecified 40% success threshold (P<0.001).

reports.label: One-month pivotal report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref published-print: March 2015; PubMed journal issue: March 2015; online day unverified
reports.citation: Richter HE, Matthews CA, Muir T, et al. "A Vaginal Bowel-Control System for the Treatment of Fecal Incontinence." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2015;125(3):540-547. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000000639
reports.followUp: One month of treatment, with an optional two-month extension

results.measure: At least 50% fewer episodes at one month among successfully fitted women entering treatment (intention to treat)
results.note: Prespecified one-sided test of success above 40% at alpha 0.025; ITT excluded 49 women who did not enter treatment after fitting assessment.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 542; Results, p 544

results.measure: At least 50% fewer episodes at one month among women with a valid treatment diary (per protocol)
results.note: Three discontinued treatment and two had fewer than seven diary days; this was a supporting analysis.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 542; Figure 2, p 543; Results, p 544

results.measure: At least 50% fewer episodes at three months among women assessed after the optional extension
results.note: Optional extension; 44 women had a three-month assessment.

No fecal incontinence episodes at one month in the per-protocol population

delivery.label: Successful fit and treatment entry
delivery.value: 61/110 women (55.5%) were successfully fitted and entered treatment.

delivery.label: Optional extension assessment
delivery.value: 48 women entered the optional two-month extension; 44 had analyzable three-month diaries.

delivery.label: Fitting attrition
delivery.value: Of 110 women entering fitting, 49 did not enter treatment: 28 unsatisfactory fit, four unable to self-manage, one lost to follow-up, two logistical or timing constraints, and 14 withdrew.

delivery.label: Insert comfort at one month
delivery.value: 54/56 per-protocol women (96.4%) reported that the insert was comfortable or could not be felt.

delivery.label: Insert sizing and fit assessment
delivery.value: Thirteen base sizes (six round, seven elliptical) were available. Fit assessment checked comfort, pubic-bone position, retention on Valsalva, and rectal occlusion with the balloon inflated.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods and Figures 2–3, p 360

delivery.label: Fitting visits
delivery.value: Up to four visits were allowed; 68/110 (61.8%) required one visit.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, pp 360–361

delivery.label: Timing of failed fitting
delivery.value: Of 49 who did not complete fitting, 16 failed initial attempts, 29 later reported displacement or discomfort, and four withdrew.
